title: Audit Procedures for Inventory
exam_relevance: HEAVILY TESTED - Expect 4-6 questions on CPA AUD exam about physical inventory observation (AU-C 501), test counts, pricing tests, obsolescence, and cutoff. Physical observation is one of the most tested specific procedures.
learning_objectives: Understand the requirement for auditor to attend physical inventory count (AU-C 501)
Know the auditor's procedures during inventory observation
Understand test counts and their purpose
Know procedures for testing inventory pricing (cost methods: FIFO, LIFO, weighted average)
Understand lower of cost or market / net realizable value testing
Know procedures for identifying obsolete, slow-moving, or damaged inventory
Understand inventory cutoff testing (purchases and sales)
Know assertions related to inventory and appropriate procedures for each

introduction.why_important: Inventory is typically material for manufacturing and retail companies. It is susceptible to theft, damage, obsolescence, and overstatement. Physical observation by the auditor is generally REQUIRED and is one of the most fundamental audit procedures.

key_standards.primary: AU-C Section 501 (Audit Evidence - Specific Considerations for Selected Items) - physical inventory observation requirements
key_standards.related: AU-C Section 330 (Performing Audit Procedures in Response to Assessed Risks)

introduction.exam_importance: Physical inventory observation requirements are HEAVILY tested. Know when observation is required, what auditor does during observation, and exceptions.

assertions_for_inventory.description: Understanding which assertions are at risk helps determine appropriate procedures

existence_occurrence.risk: Recording inventory that doesn't exist (overstatement fraud) or counting items not owned
existence_occurrence.primary_procedure: PHYSICAL OBSERVATION - observing inventory count is most reliable evidence for existence

completeness.risk: Failing to count or record all inventory (understatement)
procedures: Observe count procedures to ensure all items counted
Account for all count tags/sheets (prenumbered and controlled)
Test inventory cutoff (ensure items in transit, on consignment properly included/excluded)
Trace sample of physical items to inventory listing

rights_and_obligations.risk: Including inventory not owned (consigned goods) or excluding inventory owned but not on premises
procedures: Inquire about consigned goods (IN and OUT)
Review consignment agreements
Examine purchase documents for goods in transit (FOB terms)
Identify customer-owned items on premises
Verify proper inclusion/exclusion based on ownership
rights_and_obligations.exam_note: Goods out on consignment = INCLUDE (we own). Goods held on consignment for others = EXCLUDE (we don't own).

valuation_accuracy.risk: Inventory recorded at incorrect cost or not reduced for obsolescence/damage
procedures: Test inventory pricing (verify costs are accurate per cost method)
Test lower of cost or net realizable value
Identify and test obsolete, slow-moving, damaged inventory
Evaluate overhead allocation methods (manufacturing)
Recalculate extended amounts (quantity × price)
valuation_accuracy.exam_emphasis: Valuation is critical - inventory must be at lower of cost or NRV

procedures: Verify proper classification (raw materials, work-in-process, finished goods)
Review for pledged or assigned inventory requiring disclosure
Verify LIFO reserve disclosed if applicable
Verify obsolescence reserve disclosed

physical_inventory_observation.description: Auditor attendance at physical inventory count is a REQUIRED procedure (with limited exceptions)

general_requirement_auc_501.rule:
If inventory is MATERIAL to the financial statements, the auditor SHALL:
1. ATTEND physical inventory counting
2. OBSERVE management's count procedures
3. INSPECT the inventory
4. Perform TEST COUNTS
general_requirement_auc_501.exam_critical: Physical observation is REQUIRED when inventory is material. This is a fundamental procedure.

when_observation_required.material_inventory: If inventory is material, observation is required
when_observation_required.generally_at_year_end: Typically observe count at or near balance sheet date

interim_observation.allowed: Can observe at interim date if controls are strong
interim_observation.requirement: Must perform ROLLFORWARD procedures from observation date to year-end
rollforward_procedures: Test transactions between observation and year-end
Consider need for additional counts at year-end
interim_observation.increased_risk: Theft, error, or fraud could occur between observation and year-end

exception_1_impracticable.situation: Physical observation is IMPRACTICABLE (e.g., inventory in remote/dangerous location)
exception_1_impracticable.requirement: Perform ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURES to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence
examples_of_impracticable: Inventory stored in remote overseas location that auditor cannot access
Hazardous materials requiring special safety equipment
Inventory in war zone or dangerous area
alternative_procedures: Test controls over inventory at impracticable locations
exception_1_impracticable.may_require_scope_limitation: If cannot obtain sufficient evidence, may need to modify opinion (scope limitation)

exception_2_impossible.situation: Auditor UNABLE to attend due to timing of appointment (initial audit, appointed after year-end count already occurred)
alternative_procedures: Observe SUBSEQUENT physical count and reconcile back to year-end
Test ROLLBACK procedures (transactions from later count back to year-end)
Review client's count documentation from year-end count
exception_2_impossible.exam_scenario: Appointed as auditor in February, inventory count was December 31 - observe later count and roll back

perpetual_system.description: Detailed records updated continuously for each purchase and sale
perpetual_system.counts: Entity may perform cycle counts throughout year rather than full count at year-end
auditor_procedures: Observe and test counts (cycle counts or year-end count)
Investigate significant differences between perpetual and physical counts

periodic_system.description: Inventory determined by physical count (no detailed perpetual records)
periodic_system.counts: Must perform complete physical count at year-end
auditor_procedures: Observe and test year-end physical count (critical procedure)

auditor_procedures_during_observation.description: Specific procedures auditor performs while attending physical inventory count

review_count_plan.procedure: Review and evaluate client's physical inventory count plan and instructions
review_for: Proper use of prenumbered count tags or sheets
Procedures for identifying and handling damaged/obsolete items
Treatment of consigned goods, goods in transit
review_count_plan.weak_plan: If count plan is inadequate, auditor should suggest improvements or expand audit procedures

understand_the_inventory.procedure: Obtain understanding of inventory types, locations, and valuation methods
understand_the_inventory.tour_facilities: Tour warehouse/production facilities before count to understand layout and inventory

observe_count_procedures.procedure: Observe that client's count team is following the count plan
observe: All areas are counted and none are counted twice
Count tags are prenumbered and controlled
Damaged or obsolete items are identified and segregated
observe_count_procedures.exam_emphasis: Auditor OBSERVES - doesn't take over or perform the count for client

perform_test_counts.purpose: Verify accuracy of client's counts and document evidence

direction_1_floor_to_sheet.description: Select items from warehouse FLOOR and trace to inventory count sheets/tags
direction_1_floor_to_sheet.assertion_tested: COMPLETENESS - ensures items on floor were counted and included
direction_1_floor_to_sheet.purpose: Detect understatement - ensure all items counted

direction_2_sheet_to_floor.description: Select items from count SHEETS/TAGS and trace to warehouse floor
direction_2_sheet_to_floor.assertion_tested: EXISTENCE - ensures items listed on count sheets actually exist
direction_2_sheet_to_floor.purpose: Detect overstatement - ensure counted items really exist

perform_test_counts.documentation: Document auditor's test counts in working papers (description, location, quantity counted)
perform_test_counts.follow_up: Later, trace test counts to final inventory compilation to ensure properly included
perform_test_counts.exam_critical: Test counts in BOTH directions - floor to sheet (completeness) and sheet to floor (existence)

inspect_inventory_condition.procedure: Visually inspect inventory for condition and quality
look_for: Damaged inventory (water damage, physical damage, deterioration)
Obsolete items (old models, discontinued products, outdated technology)
Slow-moving items (dusty, stored in back, old dates)
Empty boxes or hollow squares (fraud - boxes appear full but are empty)
inspect_inventory_condition.note_for_followup: Document any damaged/obsolete items for later valuation testing (lower of cost or NRV)
inspect_inventory_condition.exam_scenario: Auditor observes damaged goods during count - should note for later writedown assessment

verify_cutoff_information.procedure: Obtain cutoff information for last shipments and last receipts before count
verify_cutoff_information.purpose: Use this information later to test sales cutoff and purchase cutoff (ensure transactions recorded in correct period)
verify_cutoff_information.exam_note: Cutoff testing uses document numbers noted during observation

account_for_prenumbered_tags_sheets.procedure: Account for all prenumbered inventory tags or count sheets
verify: All tag/sheet numbers issued are accounted for (used, voided, or unused)
Voided tags are retained and marked void (not discarded)
Unused tags are returned and controlled
account_for_prenumbered_tags_sheets.purpose: Prevent tags from being added later (fraud) or missing tags (incompleteness)
account_for_prenumbered_tags_sheets.exam_emphasis: Control over prenumbered tags is important to prevent manipulation

inquire_about_consigned_goods.procedure: Inquire about inventory held on consignment (both directions)

goods_out_on_consignment.ownership: Client owns these goods even though stored at customer location
goods_out_on_consignment.treatment: INCLUDE in client's inventory (but not counted during observation at client's facility)
goods_out_on_consignment.verification: Obtain confirmation or other evidence from consignee, review consignment agreements

goods_held_on_consignment_from_others.ownership: Others own these goods even though stored at client's location
goods_held_on_consignment_from_others.treatment: EXCLUDE from client's inventory (even though physically present)
goods_held_on_consignment_from_others.identification: Should be segregated and identified during count

inquire_about_consigned_goods.exam_trap: Goods OUT on consignment = INCLUDE. Goods IN on consignment = EXCLUDE.

observe_high_value_or_unusual_items.procedure: Pay special attention to high-value items, precious materials, or unusual items
observe_high_value_or_unusual_items.may_need_specialist: For highly specialized inventory, auditor may need to use a specialist to assess condition or quantity

obtain_final_inventory_listing.procedure: Obtain client's final compiled inventory listing
obtain_final_inventory_listing.contains: Final listing after count adjustments, priced and extended

trace_test_counts.procedure: Trace auditor's test counts from observation to final inventory listing
trace_test_counts.verify: Quantities observed by auditor agree to final listing
trace_test_counts.purpose: Ensure client didn't change quantities after count
trace_test_counts.exam_note: Must verify test counts made it to final listing unchanged

test_inventory_compilation.procedure: Test mathematical accuracy of final inventory listing

investigate_significant_adjustments.procedure: Investigate any significant adjustments made by client after the count
investigate_significant_adjustments.red_flag: Large or unusual adjustments after count may indicate count problems or manipulation
investigate_significant_adjustments.follow_up: Obtain explanations and supporting documentation for significant adjustments

inventory_pricing_testing.description: Test that inventory is properly valued according to entity's cost method

fifo_first_in_first_out.concept: Assumes oldest inventory sold first, newest inventory in ending inventory
fifo_first_in_first_out.pricing: Ending inventory priced at most recent costs
fifo_first_in_first_out.audit_procedure: Verify ending inventory quantities priced at most recent purchase costs

lifo_last_in_first_out.concept: Assumes newest inventory sold first, oldest inventory in ending inventory
lifo_last_in_first_out.pricing: Ending inventory priced at oldest costs (may be very old if inventory level stable or increasing)
lifo_last_in_first_out.audit_procedure: Verify ending inventory priced at oldest cost layers
lifo_last_in_first_out.lifo_reserve: Difference between FIFO value and LIFO value must be disclosed

weighted_average.concept: All units valued at weighted average cost
weighted_average.pricing: Ending inventory at weighted average cost per unit
weighted_average.audit_procedure: Recalculate weighted average cost and verify pricing

specific_identification.concept: Track actual cost of each specific item (used for unique, high-value items)
specific_identification.audit_procedure: Verify specific items traced to actual invoiced costs

obtain_inventory_listing.procedure: Obtain final priced inventory listing showing quantities, unit costs, and extensions
obtain_inventory_listing.contents: Includes item description, quantity, unit cost, total cost for each item

vouch_costs_to_supporting_documents.procedure: Select sample of inventory items and vouch unit costs to supporting documentation

for_purchased_items.vouch_to: Vendor invoices showing actual purchase costs
for_purchased_items.verify: Unit cost on inventory listing agrees to vendor invoice

for_manufactured_items.vouch_to: Cost accounting records showing materials, labor, and overhead
for_manufactured_items.verify: Cost calculation includes appropriate direct materials, direct labor, and allocated overhead
for_manufactured_items.overhead_allocation: Verify overhead allocation method is reasonable and consistently applied

vouch_costs_to_supporting_documents.direction: This tests valuation by verifying costs are accurately stated

test_cost_flow_assumption.procedure: Verify inventory priced according to stated cost method (FIFO, LIFO, etc.)
test_cost_flow_assumption.for_fifo: Verify ending inventory includes most recent costs (not old costs)
test_cost_flow_assumption.for_lifo: Verify ending inventory includes oldest cost layers

test_mathematical_accuracy.extensions: Recalculate quantity × unit cost for sample of items
test_mathematical_accuracy.footing: Add inventory listing and verify total agrees to general ledger

test_for_lifo_liquidation.situation: If company uses LIFO and inventory quantity decreased, old low-cost layers may be sold (LIFO liquidation)
test_for_lifo_liquidation.effect: Can artificially inflate gross margin if old low costs are matched against current revenues
test_for_lifo_liquidation.disclosure: LIFO liquidation and its effect may need disclosure if material
test_for_lifo_liquidation.audit_procedure: Compare current year quantities to prior year, calculate effect of LIFO liquidation if occurred

lower_of_cost_or_net_realizable_value.description: Inventory must be written down if net realizable value is less than cost (conservatism)

accounting_requirement.rule: Inventory must be stated at LOWER of cost or net realizable value (NRV)
accounting_requirement.cost: Historical cost per cost flow assumption (FIFO, LIFO, etc.)
accounting_requirement.net_realizable_value: Estimated selling price in ordinary course of business MINUS reasonably predictable costs of completion and disposal
accounting_requirement.if_nrv_less_than_cost: Write inventory down to NRV (record loss)
accounting_requirement.exam_note: This is GAAP requirement - market value floor

indicators_of_nrv_issues.physical_damage: Damaged inventory may not be saleable at full price
indicators_of_nrv_issues.obsolescence: Obsolete products have little or no value (discontinued models, expired items, out-of-fashion)
indicators_of_nrv_issues.slow_moving: Slow-moving inventory may need to be discounted to sell
indicators_of_nrv_issues.price_declines: Market price declined below cost (commodity prices fell)
indicators_of_nrv_issues.excess_inventory: Excess quantities may need to be sold at discount
indicators_of_nrv_issues.spoilage_perishability: Food, pharmaceuticals, chemicals may spoil or expire

identify_damaged_obsolete_slow_moving.during_observation: Note damaged or obsolete items observed during physical count
identify_damaged_obsolete_slow_moving.review_inventory_aging: Review inventory aging report (how long items have been in inventory) - old items may be obsolete
identify_damaged_obsolete_slow_moving.inquire_with_management: Ask about discontinued products, outdated models, damaged goods
identify_damaged_obsolete_slow_moving.inspect_inventory: Look for physical signs of damage, deterioration, dust (indicating slow movement)

evaluate_subsequent_sales_prices.procedure: Examine SUBSEQUENT SALES of inventory items after year-end
evaluate_subsequent_sales_prices.logic: Selling price after year-end indicates net realizable value at year-end
evaluate_subsequent_sales_prices.if_sold_below_cost: If items sold after year-end at less than cost, may indicate NRV writedown needed at year-end
evaluate_subsequent_sales_prices.exam_emphasis: Subsequent sales price is strong evidence of NRV

review_price_lists_and_catalogs.procedure: Obtain current price lists, catalogs, or online prices to estimate selling prices
review_price_lists_and_catalogs.compare: Compare selling prices to inventory costs
review_price_lists_and_catalogs.less_costs_to_sell: Subtract estimated costs of completion and disposal to determine NRV

analyze_gross_margin.procedure: Calculate gross margin percentages for products
analyze_gross_margin.red_flag: Negative or very low gross margins indicate selling price is below cost
analyze_gross_margin.by_product_line: Analyze by product line to identify problem areas

review_inventory_reserves.procedure: Review client's inventory obsolescence reserve or writedown reserve
review_inventory_reserves.evaluate_adequacy: Assess whether reserve is adequate based on identified damaged/obsolete items
review_inventory_reserves.compare_to_history: Compare reserve as % of inventory to prior years
review_inventory_reserves.develop_expectation: Auditor may develop independent estimate of required reserve

exam_scenarios.scenario_1: Auditor observes damaged inventory during count - should note for later NRV writedown assessment
exam_scenarios.scenario_2: Inventory cost is $100, selling price is $90 - must write down to $90 (NRV)
exam_scenarios.scenario_3: Subsequent sales after year-end at prices below cost indicate NRV writedown needed

cutoff_testing_for_inventory.description: Ensure purchases and sales recorded in correct period (completeness and existence)

purpose.sales_cutoff: Ensure goods sold before year-end are removed from inventory and revenue recorded. Goods sold after year-end remain in inventory.
purpose.purchase_cutoff: Ensure goods purchased and received before year-end are included in inventory and payable recorded. Goods received after year-end excluded from inventory.

obtain_last_shipping_number.procedure: During physical observation, obtain number of LAST SHIPPING DOCUMENT issued before count date
obtain_last_shipping_number.use: Use this number to test sales cutoff

test_sales_recorded_before_yearend.procedure: Select sales recorded just before year-end
test_sales_recorded_before_yearend.verify: Goods were actually shipped BEFORE year-end (not after)
test_sales_recorded_before_yearend.also_verify: Cost of goods sold was recorded (inventory reduced)
test_sales_recorded_before_yearend.red_flag: Sale recorded Dec 31 but shipped Jan 3 = improper cutoff (should be in next period, inventory should not have been reduced)

test_sales_recorded_after_yearend.procedure: Select sales recorded just after year-end
test_sales_recorded_after_yearend.verify: Goods were actually shipped AFTER year-end (not before)
test_sales_recorded_after_yearend.red_flag: Sale recorded Jan 2 but shipped Dec 29 = improper cutoff (should be in current period, inventory should have been reduced)

consider_shipping_terms.fob_shipping_point: Title passes when shipped - remove from inventory when shipped
consider_shipping_terms.fob_destination: Title passes when delivered - remove from inventory when delivered at customer

obtain_last_receiving_number.procedure: During physical observation, obtain number of LAST RECEIVING DOCUMENT issued before count date
obtain_last_receiving_number.use: Use this number to test purchase cutoff

test_purchases_recorded_before_yearend.procedure: Select purchases/payables recorded just before year-end
test_purchases_recorded_before_yearend.verify: Goods were actually RECEIVED before year-end (not after)
test_purchases_recorded_before_yearend.also_verify: Goods were included in physical inventory count
test_purchases_recorded_before_yearend.red_flag: Payable recorded Dec 31 but goods received Jan 2 = improper cutoff

test_purchases_recorded_after_yearend.procedure: Select purchases/payables recorded just after year-end
test_purchases_recorded_after_yearend.verify: Goods were actually received AFTER year-end (not before)
test_purchases_recorded_after_yearend.also_verify: Goods were excluded from physical inventory count
test_purchases_recorded_after_yearend.red_flag: Payable recorded Jan 2 but goods received Dec 30 = improper cutoff (should be in current period)

goods_in_transit.situation: Goods shipped by vendor but not yet received by client at year-end
goods_in_transit.fob_shipping_point: Client owns goods in transit - INCLUDE in inventory and record payable
goods_in_transit.fob_destination: Vendor owns goods in transit - EXCLUDE from inventory and no payable
goods_in_transit.audit_procedure: Review shipping terms (FOB) for goods in transit at year-end, verify proper inclusion/exclusion
goods_in_transit.exam_critical: FOB shipping point in transit at year-end = client includes in inventory

inventory_turnover_ratio.calculation: Cost of goods sold ÷ Average inventory
inventory_turnover_ratio.interpretation: Higher ratio = faster turnover. Lower than expected may indicate excess or obsolete inventory.
inventory_turnover_ratio.comparison: Compare to prior years and industry

days_inventory_on_hand.interpretation: Number of days inventory sits before being sold. Higher than expected may indicate slow-moving or excess inventory.

gross_margin_percentage.interpretation: Should be relatively stable. Significant changes may indicate pricing issues, inventory valuation problems, or cutoff errors.
gross_margin_percentage.by_product_line: Negative gross margin indicates selling below cost (NRV writedown needed)

use_of_specialists.when_needed: For highly technical, specialized, or unique inventory
examples: Chemicals or pharmaceuticals (need scientist to assess quality/usability)
Complex work-in-process (need engineer to assess completion percentage)
use_of_specialists.auditor_responsibility: Evaluate specialist's qualifications, objectivity, and work

inventory_at_locations_not_visited.situation: Inventory stored at multiple locations - auditor cannot visit all locations
procedures: Visit locations with material amounts
For other locations: test controls, perform analytical procedures, consider confirming with third-party warehouses
Assess risk of material misstatement at unvisited locations

audit_procedures: CONFIRM inventory quantities and condition with third party (send confirmation)
Assess third party's controls and reputation
inventory_held_by_third_parties.exam_note: Confirmation with third-party warehouse is primary procedure for inventory held by others

problem_1.question:
An auditor observes the client's physical inventory count on December 31. The auditor notes the last shipping document number as #5280 and the last receiving document number as #8450. When testing cutoff, the auditor selects voucher #8455 (recorded in January) and finds the receiving report is dated December 30. What should the auditor conclude?

A) The transaction is properly recorded because the voucher was recorded after the receiving report date.

B) The transaction represents a cutoff error - the purchase should have been recorded in December and inventory should have been increased.

C) No adjustment needed if the amount is immaterial.

D) The auditor should verify whether the goods were included in the physical count before determining if adjustment is needed.
problem_1.explanation:
This is a PURCHASE CUTOFF error. The goods were RECEIVED on December 30 (before year-end), but the payable was recorded in January (after year-end). Goods received before year-end should be: (1) included in December's inventory, and (2) recorded as a December payable. Since the last receiving number during observation was #8450, receiving #8455 (dated Dec 30) occurred BEFORE the count but was likely not counted (it came after #8450). This is a cutoff error requiring adjustment.

D is not the best answer because the receiving date (Dec 30) clearly indicates this should be in December regardless of whether it was counted - if not counted, both inventory and payables are understated.
problem_1.exam_tip: Purchase cutoff: If goods RECEIVED before year-end, should INCLUDE in inventory and RECORD payable, regardless of when invoice processed.

problem_2.question:
Which of the following best describes the auditor's primary purpose in performing test counts during observation of the client's physical inventory?

A) To determine the value of inventory for financial statement purposes.

B) To provide evidence that the client's count procedures are accurate and that the auditor attended the count.

C) To detect all errors in the inventory count.

D) To eliminate the need for the auditor to test inventory pricing.
problem_2.explanation:
Test counts serve TWO primary purposes: (1) provide EVIDENCE of the accuracy of the client's count procedures, and (2) DOCUMENT that the auditor actually attended and observed the physical count. The auditor documents specific test counts in working papers and later traces them to the final inventory listing.

A is wrong - test counts address quantities/existence, not valuation (pricing is tested separately).
C is wrong - test counts are samples, not designed to detect ALL errors.
D is wrong - test counts don't eliminate need for pricing tests (separate procedure).
problem_2.exam_tip: Test counts = evidence of count accuracy + documentation of auditor attendance. Must test in BOTH directions (floor to sheet and sheet to floor).

problem_3.question:
During observation of inventory, the auditor notes several items that appear dusty and are stored in the back of the warehouse. The manufacturing dates on the items indicate they are over two years old. What should the auditor do?

A) Immediately propose an adjustment to write down these items to zero.

B) Note these items for subsequent follow-up testing regarding obsolescence and net realizable value.

C) Exclude these items from test counts since they appear to be obsolete.

D) Request that the client remove these items from inventory during the count.
problem_3.explanation:
The auditor should NOTE these items during observation for LATER FOLLOW-UP regarding obsolescence and net realizable value testing. These are indicators of potentially slow-moving or obsolete inventory that may require writedown, but the auditor needs to: (1) examine subsequent sales to see if items sold (and at what price), (2) review price lists, (3) evaluate NRV, (4) assess client's obsolescence reserve. The observation is the first step - noting items for later testing.

A is wrong - cannot immediately propose writedown to zero without further testing.
C is wrong - should still test count these items (they may have some value).
D is wrong - not auditor's role to direct client to remove items; auditor evaluates client's count and later tests valuation.
problem_3.exam_tip: During observation, NOTE damaged/obsolete/slow-moving items for LATER NRV testing. Don't propose adjustments on the spot - need to evaluate NRV first.

problem_4.question:
Which of the following situations would allow an auditor to OMIT observation of physical inventory?

A) The client requests that the auditor not attend because it will disrupt operations.

B) Inventory is immaterial to the financial statements.

C) The client has strong internal controls over inventory.

D) The auditor confirmed inventory with third parties who hold the inventory.
problem_4.explanation:
Physical observation is REQUIRED when inventory is MATERIAL. Therefore, observation may be omitted if inventory is IMMATERIAL to the financial statements. The other valid reasons for omitting observation are: (1) impracticable (dangerous/remote location) with alternative procedures, or (2) impossible due to timing (appointed after count occurred) with alternative procedures.

A is wrong - client preference is NOT a valid reason to omit observation.
C is wrong - strong controls alone don't eliminate observation requirement (though may affect extent).
D is wrong - confirmation doesn't substitute for observation requirement (though it's a useful supplemental procedure for inventory held by third parties).
problem_4.exam_tip: Observation required when inventory material. Exceptions: immaterial, impracticable, or impossible (with alternative procedures). Client preference is NEVER a valid reason.

problem_5.question:
At December 31, Client owns goods in transit that were shipped FOB shipping point on December 28 and are expected to arrive January 3. How should these goods be treated?

A) Exclude from inventory because not physically present at year-end.

B) Include in inventory and record the related payable because title passed when shipped.

C) Exclude from inventory but record the payable.

D) Wait until goods arrive in January to record both inventory and payable.
problem_5.explanation:
FOB SHIPPING POINT means title (ownership) passes to buyer when goods are SHIPPED by the seller. Since goods shipped December 28 (before year-end), the client OWNS the goods at December 31 even though not physically present. Therefore: (1) INCLUDE in inventory at December 31, and (2) RECORD payable at December 31.

A is wrong - physical presence doesn't determine ownership; FOB terms do.
C is wrong - if recording payable (because client owns goods), must also include in inventory.
D is wrong - incorrect timing; should record when title passes (Dec 28) not when physically received.
problem_5.exam_tip: FOB SHIPPING POINT in transit = buyer owns = include in buyer's inventory. FOB DESTINATION in transit = seller owns = exclude from buyer's inventory.

tip_1_observation_required.rule: Physical observation is REQUIRED when inventory is material
tip_1_observation_required.exceptions: Immaterial, Impracticable (with alternatives), or Impossible due to timing (with alternatives)
tip_1_observation_required.not_valid_reasons: Client preference, cost, time, or inconvenience
tip_1_observation_required.exam_question: When can auditor omit observation? Must be one of the valid reasons

tip_2_test_counts_both_directions.direction_1: Floor to sheet = tests COMPLETENESS (all items on floor were counted)
tip_2_test_counts_both_directions.direction_2: Sheet to floor = tests EXISTENCE (items on sheets actually exist)
tip_2_test_counts_both_directions.purpose: Provide evidence of count accuracy + document auditor attendance
tip_2_test_counts_both_directions.follow_up: Trace test counts to final inventory listing to verify included unchanged

tip_3_auditor_observes_not_counts.clarification: Auditor OBSERVES client's count procedures - doesn't perform count for client
tip_3_auditor_observes_not_counts.auditor_does_not: Take over the count or perform complete count

tip_4_cutoff_testing.obtain_numbers: During observation, note LAST SHIPPING # and LAST RECEIVING #
tip_4_cutoff_testing.sales_cutoff: Test transactions before/after year-end - verify shipped in correct period per FOB terms
tip_4_cutoff_testing.purchase_cutoff: Test transactions before/after year-end - verify received in correct period
tip_4_cutoff_testing.fob_shipping_point_in_transit: Buyer owns = include in buyer's inventory + record payable
tip_4_cutoff_testing.fob_destination_in_transit: Seller owns = exclude from buyer's inventory

tip_5_consigned_goods.goods_out_on_consignment: Client owns (even though at customer location) = INCLUDE in client's inventory
tip_5_consigned_goods.goods_in_on_consignment: Others own (even though at client location) = EXCLUDE from client's inventory
tip_5_consigned_goods.exam_trap: Physically present doesn't mean owned. Check ownership!

tip_6_nrv_testing.requirement: Inventory at LOWER of cost or net realizable value
tip_6_nrv_testing.nrv: Estimated selling price MINUS costs of completion/disposal
tip_6_nrv_testing.indicators: Damaged, obsolete, slow-moving, price declines, excess quantities
tip_6_nrv_testing.best_evidence: SUBSEQUENT SALES prices after year-end indicate NRV
tip_6_nrv_testing.procedure: Note damaged/obsolete during observation, then test NRV later

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: When can auditor omit inventory observation?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Immaterial, Impracticable with alternatives, or Impossible with alternatives. NOT client preference.

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: What is purpose of test counts?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Evidence of count accuracy + documentation of attendance. Test BOTH directions (floor to sheet AND sheet to floor).

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: Cutoff scenario with dates and document numbers
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Compare receiving/shipping dates to year-end. Consider FOB terms. Verify recorded in correct period.

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: FOB shipping point vs FOB destination - who owns goods in transit?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: FOB shipping point = buyer owns when shipped. FOB destination = seller owns until delivered.
Goods OUT on consignment = INCLUDE (we own). Goods IN on consignment = EXCLUDE (others own).
Note for later NRV testing. Examine subsequent sales, price lists, evaluate writedown.

memorization_aids.test_counts_directions: Floor to Sheet = Completeness. Sheet to Floor = Existence.
memorization_aids.consigned_goods: OUT = OUR inventory (include). IN = others' Inventory (exclude).
memorization_aids.fob_terms: FOB Shipping = buyer owns when Shipped. FOB Destination = buyer owns when Delivered.

key_concepts: Physical observation is REQUIRED when inventory is material (AU-C 501)
Exceptions to observation: immaterial, impracticable, or impossible (with alternative procedures)
Test counts in BOTH directions: floor to sheet (completeness) and sheet to floor (existence)
Auditor OBSERVES count procedures - doesn't perform count for client
During observation: observe procedures, perform test counts, inspect condition, obtain cutoff info, account for tags
Trace test counts to final inventory listing to verify included unchanged
Cutoff testing: note last shipping/receiving numbers, test transactions before and after year-end
FOB shipping point in transit = buyer owns (include in inventory). FOB destination = seller owns until delivered.
Consigned goods OUT = include (we own). Consigned goods IN = exclude (others own).
Inventory at lower of cost or NRV - examine subsequent sales, identify damaged/obsolete items
Pricing tests: vouch costs to invoices, verify cost method applied correctly, test extensions
Analytical procedures: inventory turnover, days on hand, gross margin analysis
critical_for_exam: Physical observation REQUIRED when material (heavily tested)
Know THREE exceptions: immaterial, impracticable, impossible
Test counts in BOTH directions (floor to sheet AND sheet to floor)
Cutoff testing: use last shipping/receiving numbers from observation
FOB shipping point in transit = buyer includes in inventory
Consigned goods: OUT = include, IN = exclude
Lower of cost or NRV - subsequent sales is best evidence
Auditor maintains control over observations (like confirmations)
common_mistakes: Thinking client preference is valid reason to omit observation (NO - must be immaterial, impracticable, or impossible)
Thinking auditor performs the complete count (NO - auditor observes and does test counts)
Testing counts in only one direction (NO - must test BOTH floor to sheet AND sheet to floor)
Not considering FOB terms for goods in transit (critical for ownership)
Thinking goods held on premises are always owned (NO - consigned goods IN are excluded)
Thinking goods off premises are not owned (NO - consigned goods OUT are included)
Not obtaining cutoff information during observation (needed for later cutoff tests)
